title: Internal module normalization and exact closed-test unit evaluation
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and on every small pro-etale site put $\Lambda_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use internal $\Lambda_Y$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], their exact inverse images and ordinary unbounded derived direct images computed on K-injectives [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. All sites and section values are taken in a common sufficiently large universe. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak a\subseteq A$ an ideal, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $s:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak a)\hookrightarrow U$. Let $v$ be the affine ind-etale closed-site lift [def-exc-closed-site-lift]. Let $V\to Z$ be an affine ind-etale object such that $V$ and $B=v(V)$ are w-contractible [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. For each scheme $Y$, reconstruct the section-ring sheaf $R_Y$ of $\Lambda_Y$ and let $E_Y:\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_Y}\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_Y)$ be the equivalence preserving underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Then $E_Y$ and its termwise extension preserve exact sequences, quasi-isomorphisms and K-injective complexes; the ordinary module inverse images and direct images are identified with the internal ones, including their units and counits. In particular a module inverse image has the ordinary abelian inverse image as underlying sheaf, and $(b_*F)(W)=F(Y'\times_YW)$ for $b:Y'\to Y$.
The objects $V$ and $B$ are weakly contractible in their ambient full pro-etale sites and affine ind-etale basis sites: every epimorphism of set sheaves is surjective on their sections. The identity object of the affine ind-etale site of $B$ has this property too. Evaluation at $V$ and $B$ on module sheaves preserves homology. The closed immersion $V=B\times_UZ\hookrightarrow B$ has every point of $B$ specializing into $V$, and the counit of its canonical lift/base-change adjunction at the identity of $B$ is invertible. For every internal module $F$ on $U$, the actual adjunction-unit map
$$u_{F,V}:F(B)\longrightarrow(s^*F)(V),\quad x\longmapsto s^{-1}x$$
[def-sfb-proetale-inverse-image-unit-section] is an isomorphism of $\Lambda_U(B)$-modules, where the target action is through $\Lambda_U(B)\to\Lambda_Z(V)$. Its inverse is the closed-evaluation identification, and $u_{F,V}$ is natural in $F$ and in maps of such test objects.

proof.text: Use the recorded additive internal/section-module equivalence. Equivalences preserve finite limits and colimits, hence homology; their termwise functors do also. The existing equivalence instance preserves K-injective complexes in both directions, and homology preservation implies preservation of quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; application to the exact equivalence and its inverse

proof.text: The internal upper-star already preserves homology. Its underlying abelian inverse-image comparison is the extension/restriction-of-scalars isomorphism for the invertible condensed coefficient pullback. The extension-unit coherence equation shows that this comparison sends the actual internal unit to the abelian unit. The adjunct of the forgotten ordinary module unit is invertible by the unit-comparison theorem; compose its inverse with the internal comparison to obtain q. The canonical ordinary adjunction unit has exactly inverseSection as its section map, so the two unit equations prove the required normalization. The recorded operation-transport theorem supplies the internal/section-module unit and counit equations. Direct-image sections agree definitionally.

Apply the source weak-contractibility theorem using each affine test's canonical isomorphism to the spectrum of its global sections. Convert epimorphisms into locally surjective maps. Restriction to the affine pro-etale basis is already an equivalence of sheaf categories. Apply its inverse to a basis epimorphism, lift sections on the full site, then transport the lift through the counit isomorphism. Apply the same argument to the identity affine test over the lifted scheme.

Apply weakly contractible module evaluation exactness to the reconstructed section rings at V and its lift. Internal abelian evaluation is definitionally the composite of the internal/section-module equivalence, ordinary module evaluation, and the forgetful functor from modules to abelian groups. Each preserves homology, proving both internal evaluation assertions.

source.place: Tag 0946, lemma-w-contractible (1), with sites-modules Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian

proof.text: The closed-site functor properties give the closed immersion, pullback square, and specialization of every point into V. Transport specialization into quotient coordinates using the closed immersion's global-section quotient. The identity test of the spectrum of the lifted scheme's global sections is weakly contractible. The specialization closed-site counit theorem then applies to every supplied lift/base-change adjunction.

source.place: Tag 09BK, lemma-closed-immersion-affines; Tag 09AC, closed specialization argument as recorded in the cited counit lemma

proof.text: Apply the abelian specialization-unit theorem to the original quotient immersion and the lifted full-site affine test. Its specialization hypothesis follows from the recorded pullback isomorphism. The internal/abelian comparison's unit equation then makes the actual internal unit component invertible. Restriction along the canonical fibre isomorphism is invertible as well; their composite is precisely unitSection. Form its additive equivalence. For scalar compatibility, apply the internal/section-module equivalence to the actual unit and compose with the identity-on-sections lower comparison. This is a linear module morphism. Its sectionwise linearity followed by semilinearity of restriction along the fibre isomorphism proves the displayed scalarSection equation.

source.place: Tags 03D2 and 03D3, module inverse-image adjunction and its linear unit; proetale Tag 09AC

proof.text: Use the explicit siteHomMap adjunction for closed lift and base change. Its unit maps under the affine-basis inclusion to the canonical fibre isomorphism. Precomposition by the lift followed by abelian sheafification is left adjoint to base-change pushforward on the basis. The full-site abelian inverse-image adjunction and the two basis restriction equivalences have an identity square of right adjoints. Its inverse mate is invertible. The mate unit equation, the explicit precomposition adjunction, and the sheafification hom equivalence show that this comparison sends a sheafification-unit section to the actual abelian-unit section restricted along the fibre isomorphism. Compose with the internal/abelian comparison to construct c with its required equation. Apply c to the two candidate inverse images of a section: bijectivity of unitSection and the iso identities identify the inverse with closed evaluation. Naturality in modules follows from c and the sheafification unit; naturality in tests follows from their presheaf naturality.

Step 4: weakly-contractible-evaluation-exact applies at B and at V. Step 5: the 09BK node plus the specialization counit lemma over Spec O(B) with test object id_B. Step 6: module-specialization-unit at B, needing projectivity (Step 3) and specialization into V (Step 5), and its unit is the unit-section definition after alpha_s. Step 7: (vV, eta_V) is initial in I_V, 09BL(2) makes the canonical sheafification map an isomorphism at weakly contractible V, and conjugate-unit uniqueness carries the basis unit to the full-site unit, which gives both naturalities. Edge cases checked: ideal 0, unit ideal (Z and V empty), zero ring. No hypothesis is added and no target is weakened.
